summary: Describes additions to ARP that let a station request the protocol address matching a given hardware address, the reverse of normal ARP. It is a draft standard.

eli5.summary: Instead of knowing the address and asking who it is, you know who it is and ask what its address is.

questions: how does inarp work in frame relay
subtitle: ARP run backwards: given a hardware address, ask the station behind it for its protocol address.

tldr.problem: A Frame Relay station may learn of a new virtual circuit and its DLCI, which acts as a hardware address, without knowing the protocol address of the station at the other end, so the circuit is unusable.
tldr.mechanism: Inverse ARP reuses the ARP packet format with new operation codes (8 for request, 9 for response). The requester sends the request directly on the circuit with the target protocol address zero filled, and the other side answers with its own address.
tldr.outcome: It replaces RFC 1293 and adds a packet diagram, an example and a security section. It adds no authentication, so ARP's known weaknesses still apply.

today: RFC 2390 is a Draft Standard that obsoletes RFC 1293, and the unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. It states that it adds no security mechanisms beyond those of ARP.

sections.title: The Problem Inverse ARP Solves
sections.content:
In Frame Relay, permanent virtual circuits (PVCs) are identified by a Data Link Connection Identifier (DLCI), which can be thought of as the Frame Relay equivalent of a hardware address. A network may announce a new circuit and its DLCI through signaling messages, but the announcement does not include a protocol address. The station knows the connection exists but cannot address the other side, so the circuit is unusable without new configuration or a discovery mechanism.

Other approaches were rejected. Reverse ARP returns the protocol address of the requester, not of the station receiving the request. IP-specific mechanisms would not resolve other protocols. So ARP itself was expanded. InARP is more efficient than sending ARP messages on every circuit for every address, and more flexible than static configuration. It is not limited to Frame Relay and may be used in any network that provides destination hardware addresses without matching protocol addresses.
sections.eli5: You have a phone line to someone, but nobody told you who picks up. Inverse ARP is how you ask them to say who they are.

sections.title: The Packet Format and Operation Codes
sections.content:
Inverse ARP is an extension of ARP and uses the same packet format: hardware type (ar$hrd, 16 bits), protocol type (ar$pro, 16 bits), hardware address length (ar$hln, 8 bits), protocol address length (ar$pln, 8 bits), operation code (ar$op, 16 bits), then the source and target hardware and protocol addresses. Valid hardware and protocol type values are the same as for ARP.

The operation code is 8 for an InARP request and 9 for an InARP response, chosen not to conflict with other ARP extensions. Address lengths depend on the environment. For IP over Frame Relay the hardware address length is 2, 3 or 4 and the protocol address length is 4.
sections.eli5: It uses the same form as ARP, with two new tick boxes: one for asking and one for answering.

sections.title: How a Request and Response Work
sections.content:
InARP works like ARP except that it does not broadcast, because the destination hardware address is already known. When an interface supporting InARP becomes active, it should send a request on each active PVC for which InARP is active. The requester fills in its own source hardware and protocol addresses and the known target hardware address, zero fills the target protocol address, and sends the packet directly to the target.

A receiving station may add the requester's mapping to its ARP cache. Unlike other ARP requests, it may assume any InARP request is meant for it. It should reply, using the request's source addresses as the response's target addresses. If it is unable or unwilling, it ignores the request. The requester may then complete its ARP table entry. As with ARP, learned information may be aged or invalidated.

A multi-addressed host, with several protocol addresses on one interface, must pick one to answer with: the one matching the network of the requester, such as the same subnet for IP. If it has no suitable address it should not respond. It should also send one request per address defined on the interface, though the other side may answer some or none.
sections.eli5: You tap on the line and say who you are. The other side, knowing the tap was for them, says who they are in reply.

sections.title: InARP over Frame Relay
sections.content:
On a Frame Relay interface that signals DLCIs, a station sends an InARP request addressed to the new circuit. Packets use the NLPID/SNAP encapsulation from RFC 1490, with control 0x03, NLPID 0x80, OUI 0x00 00 00 and PID 0x08 06. In the request, ar$hrd is 0x000F (Frame Relay), ar$pro is the protocol being searched for (IP is 0x0800), ar$op is 8, ar$sha is the requester's Q.922 address, ar$tha is the Q.922 address of the new circuit, and ar$tpa is 0. The response is built similarly with ar$op 9 and the requested address in ar$spa.

DLCIs mostly have only local significance, and the network changes the DLCI as a frame crosses it. In the RFC's Figure 1, A sends on DLCI 50 and B sees DLCI 70. So the hardware addresses inside the packet are not valid on arrival, but the address in the frame header is. The receiving Frame Relay interface may copy the header address into the source hardware address, and the target hardware address may be zero filled or ignored. As a result, the interface only needs to intervene when processing incoming packets.
sections.eli5: The number on a phone line looks different from each end. So instead of trusting the number written on the note, each side reads the number from the line the note arrived on.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: InARP is a functional enhancement to the ARP family and has the same security constraints. ARP has no authentication, so there are known issues such as host impersonation. This document adds no new security mechanisms to the ARP family.
sections.eli5: Anyone can answer the call and claim to be someone else, and nothing here checks whether they are telling the truth.

items.label: InARP request
items.desc: Asks the station on a known hardware address for its protocol address.

viz.caption: INARP REQUEST AND RESPONSE FOR FIGURE 1 (RFC 2390)

messages.label: InARP request (op 8)
messages.note: Target hardware address is DLCI 50 (0x0C21); target protocol address unknown. B sees the sender as DLCI 70 (0x1061).

messages.label: InARP response (op 9)
messages.note: Carries B's protocol address pB and A's address pA; A reads the source hardware address from the frame header.
